groups.title: INPUTS — Room Image + Mask + Texture Tile

info.name: Texture Changer — IPAdapter Texture Transfer (SDXL 8GB)
info.description: Applies material/texture from a user-uploaded tile/pattern image onto detected room surfaces using IPAdapter style transfer + masked SDXL inpainting. The uploaded texture image is used as IPAdapter reference with attn_mask so it ONLY affects the masked surface region. The text prompt reinforces the texture type. This creates a tiled/repeating pattern look because IPAdapter transfers the visual style (color, pattern, grain) while SDXL adapts it to the surface geometry and perspective.
info.author: Removation Pipeline

inputs.surface_mask: Node 2 — Binary mask (white = apply texture, black = preserve)
inputs.texture_tile: Node 17 — User-uploaded texture/tile/pattern image (e.g. a single tile, carpet swatch, marble sample)

outputs.texture/result: Room image with texture applied to masked surface

dynamic_nodes.node_2: LoadImage — surface mask filename injected by orchestrator

ipadapter_settings.rationale: Style transfer weight type ensures the texture pattern/color/grain is transferred without transferring spatial composition. Weight 0.85 gives strong texture adherence while letting SDXL handle perspective correction. For subtle textures (marble, concrete) lower to 0.70. For bold patterns (tiles, wallpaper) keep at 0.85-1.0.
ipadapter_settings.attn_mask: Surface mask is passed as attn_mask so IPAdapter ONLY influences the masked region — furniture/floor/ceiling outside mask stays untouched

sampling.rationale: CFG lowered to 7.5 (from 8.0) because IPAdapter already provides strong visual guidance — high CFG + IPAdapter can cause oversaturation. Denoise 0.88 provides enough room for texture application while preserving room geometry.

info.how_tiling_works: IPAdapter transfers the visual STYLE (texture pattern, color, grain) from the reference tile image. SDXL then generates that style within the masked area, naturally adapting it to the surface geometry and perspective. The result looks like the texture was applied as repeating tiles because IPAdapter embeds the pattern at a high level — it doesn't care about tile boundaries, it transfers the overall visual character.

tuning_tips.texture_too_aggressive: Lower IPAdapter weight to 0.6-0.7 and/or reduce denoise to 0.75
tuning_tips.colors_wrong: Add specific color terms to positive prompt like '(warm honey brown:1.2)'
tuning_tips.pattern_not_repeating_enough: Add '(seamless repeating pattern:1.3), (tiled texture:1.2)' to prompt
tuning_tips.texture_bleeding_outside_mask: Check mask quality — regenerate with tighter CLIPSeg threshold
tuning_tips.oom_crash: Try IPAdapterUnifiedLoader preset 'PLUS (high strength)' → 'LIGHT' for smaller model
